subject: Computer Networking
title: Layer 3 Switches
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Layer 3 Switches.

hook.text: What if a switch could also route? Layer 3 switches combine switching speed with routing intelligence.

buildup.text: Normal switches use MAC addresses. Layer 3 switches also understand IPs and route between VLANs.

discovery.text: They route between networks at wire speed in hardware — much faster than a software router.

twist.text: They can't fully replace routers. They lack WAN features, NAT, and advanced firewall capabilities.

climax.text: In campuses, Layer 3 switches handle inter-VLAN routing while routers handle the internet edge.

punchline.text: Layer 3 switches route at switch speed. Best of both worlds.

quiz.question: What extra capability does a Layer 3 switch have over a Layer 2 switch?
options: It can route traffic between different IP subnets
It can compress data before sending

details.summary: Layer 3 switches combine the wire-speed forwarding of a traditional switch with the routing capabilities of a router, making inter-VLAN routing decisions in hardware ASICs.
details.whyItMatters: Layer 3 switches eliminate the bottleneck of routing inter-VLAN traffic through a separate router. They are the backbone of modern campus and data center networks.
takeaways: Layer 3 switches route between VLANs using hardware ASICs
Inter-VLAN routing at wire speed eliminates router bottlenecks
They replace separate routers for internal network routing

faq.question: When should you use a Layer 3 switch instead of a router?
faq.answer: Use Layer 3 switches for fast inter-VLAN routing within a campus or data center. Use routers for WAN connections, internet access, VPN termination, and complex policy-based routing. Most networks use Layer 3 switches for internal traffic and routers at the network edge.

faq.question: Can a Layer 3 switch replace a router entirely?
faq.answer: Not usually. Layer 3 switches excel at high-speed internal routing but typically lack WAN interfaces, NAT, full BGP support, and advanced firewall features that edge routers provide. They complement routers by handling the bulk of internal traffic while routers manage external connectivity.
